{"id":"persona-5s4b.89","title":"Missing doc comments on public items and modules","description":"rust.md: "Put a doc comment on everything that rustdoc knows how to document. No exceptions, not even for module-private items." Most of persona-core follows this; persona-grpc largely does not.

Modules with no `//!` header:
- persona-grpc/src/server.rs
- persona-grpc/src/service.rs
- persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs
- persona-attestors/src/registry.rs
- persona-core/src/trust_bundle.rs

Undocumented public items:
- persona-grpc/src/service.rs:16-20 — `WorkloadApiService` and all three of its `pub` fields (`signer`, `bundles`, `attestors`); line 23 `new()`
- persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs:84-93 — `AttestError` and its three variants
- persona-core/src/signer.rs:16-25 — `SignerError` and its four variants
- persona-core/src/trust_bundle.rs:9 — the `trust_domain` field (the other two fields are documented); line 41 `TrustBundleStore::new()`
- persona-attestors — `new()` on all eight attestors (ssh.rs:27, oidc.rs:22, tailscale.rs:22, gpg.rs:17, did_key.rs:18, fido2.rs:27, goa.rs:22, piv.rs:20); `TailscaleAttestor::is_available` (tailscale.rs:28) — the other seven `is_available` fns are documented

Panics sections missing on functions that can panic (rust.md requires these on any caller-triggerable panic):
- persona-core/src/trust_bundle.rs:46, 55, 65 — `upsert`, `snapshot` and `get` all `.expect("trust bundle lock poisoned")`. A poisoned lock is another thread's bug, not the caller's, so per rust.md this is arguably not a public panic condition — but then the `.expect` should just be `.unwrap()`, since `PoisonError` already says exactly that. rust.md names poisoned mutex as the canonical case for bare `.unwrap()`.
- persona-core/src/signer.rs:98 — `sign_jwt_svid` panics on a pre-epoch system clock.

This is a single mechanical pass, hence one issue.","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:40.007789796Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:40.007789796Z","labels":["rust","docs","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.89","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T21:00:40.029751313Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"description":"Scoped to the panic-documentation points; the broader missing-docs sweep is persona-5s4b.78.

rust.md: functions that can panic need a `## Panics` section, but it "documents only caller-triggerable conditions — panics a caller at the item's visibility can cause while respecting its contract", and a poisoned mutex is the canonical case for a bare `.unwrap()` because `PoisonError` already explains itself.

Three sites in persona-core/src/trust_bundle.rs use `.expect("trust bundle lock poisoned")`: `upsert` (:50), `snapshot` (:58) and `get` (:69). The message adds nothing that `PoisonError`'s own Display does not already say, so per rust.md these should be plain `.unwrap()`. A poisoned lock here means another thread panicked while holding it — our bug, not the caller's — so it correctly gets no `## Panics` section either. Right now the three `.expect` strings imply a documented contract that is not documented anywhere.

persona-core/src/signer.rs:98-100 is the opposite case and is handled correctly:

    .expect("system clock before epoch")

That one states an invariant the `Err` does not carry, so `.expect` is right — but `sign_jwt_svid` has no `## Panics` section saying a pre-epoch clock aborts issuance. It is environment-triggerable rather than argument-triggerable, so it belongs in the doc as a "may panic if".

Fix: drop the three `.expect` messages in trust_bundle.rs to `.unwrap()`, and add a `## Panics` line to `sign_jwt_svid`.","priority":3,"title":"Panics-section and lock-poisoning expect() treatment is inconsistent"}
